stories.body: Iran said the 60-day deadline in its memorandum of understanding with the United States had become null and void because of what Tehran called Washington's violations. The dispute comes as the Strait of Hormuz has remained largely closed during the US-Iran war, disrupting a route normally used by about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments. Iranian officials said they were close to an arrangement with Oman on a transit route through the strait, while President Donald Trump rejected extending the memorandum and reportedly threatened Oman if it obstructed US-led talks. Tehran denied Trump's claim that Washington had a direct backchannel to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
stories.headline: Iran declares US negotiation memorandum deadline void as Strait of Hormuz tensions rise

stories.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US envoy Jared Kushner held lengthy talks on Gaza but made no breakthrough on the sequencing of an Israeli withdrawal and Hamas's disarmament. Netanyahu maintained that Israeli forces would not withdraw or allow reconstruction until Hamas had fully surrendered its weapons, and the sides discussed having a US general verify the process. Hamas has said it accepts a US-backed roadmap that includes disarmament, withdrawal and an end to attacks, but Israel insists disarmament must come first. Kushner said reconstruction would not proceed before demilitarisation and that the US would not restrict Israel's right to respond to imminent threats.
stories.headline: Netanyahu and Kushner discuss US oversight of Hamas disarmament as Gaza talks remain stalled

stories.body: Russia's Supreme Court rejected Yabloko's appeal against its exclusion from September's parliamentary election, leaving the country's only registered party explicitly opposing the war in Ukraine off the ballot. The ruling followed a case brought by the pro-Kremlin Rodina party and comes amid a broader crackdown on dissent. On the same day, a court in Pskov sentenced Yabloko deputy leader Lev Shlosberg to 11 years and one month in a penal colony on charges of discrediting the armed forces and spreading false information about them. Police detained dozens of supporters and journalists outside the court, while Yabloko said it would seek further review.
stories.headline: Russia's Supreme Court upholds exclusion of anti-war party Yabloko from elections

stories.body: A student opened fire at a Catholic junior high school associated with Ateneo de Zamboanga University in the southern Philippine city of Zamboanga, killing another student before taking his own life, officials said. Police said the suspected ninth-grade gunman brought a pistol and rifle onto the campus and fired in a classroom; the victim was a student one grade above him. The mayor said the attacker had first fired at a teacher and missed. Authorities said there was no longer an active threat and were investigating the motive, as purported livestream footage of the attack circulated online.
stories.headline: Two students die in shooting at a Philippine Catholic school

stories.body: Zambia's electoral commission declared President Hakainde Hichilema the winner of a second five-year term, with about 61.4% of valid votes against 38% for his main challenger, Brian Mundubile. Hichilema, 64, campaigned on economic recovery and debt restructuring but faces pressure to create jobs and reduce poverty. The election was followed by allegations of fraud, arrests of opposition figures and a temporary suspension of counting after reports of violence and stolen ballot papers. European Union observers said voting was broadly peaceful but that the wider process was affected by restricted freedoms, legal uncertainty and unequal campaign conditions.
stories.headline: Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema wins a second term

stories.body: The Trump administration temporarily halted construction of a border project in Texas's Big Bend National Park while Customs and Border Protection commissioner Rodney Scott conducts an on-the-ground assessment. The project has drawn bipartisan criticism from opponents who say it would damage a remote, environmentally sensitive landscape where rugged terrain and historically low crossing numbers already deter migration. Scott said he would meet local leaders, community members and other stakeholders, though CBP did not say how long the pause would last. The administration has been advancing border-wall construction using $46 billion approved by Congress and regulatory waivers.
stories.headline: Trump administration pauses contentious border construction in Texas' Big Bend National Park

stories.body: Luigi Mangione's New York state murder trial in the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson has been postponed indefinitely after he pleaded guilty to federal stalking charges and admitted shooting Thompson in Manhattan in 2024. The state trial had been due to begin on September 8, but the judge gave Manhattan prosecutors until October 9 to answer Mangione's claim that New York's protections against double jeopardy bar a second prosecution for the same conduct. A hearing is scheduled for December 10, shortly before his federal sentencing on December 18. Prosecutors oppose dismissing the state case, in which Mangione has pleaded not guilty to charges including second-degree murder.
stories.headline: Luigi Mangione's New York state murder trial postponed amid double-jeopardy dispute

stories.body: Tropical Storm Lala left one person dead and caused extensive flooding, wind damage and power outages across Hawaii after weakening from a Category 1 hurricane. More than 100,000 customers remained without electricity, while some reports put the number of affected households above 200,000. On the Big Island, flash floods, mudslides, uprooted trees and washed-out roads isolated remote communities, and officials said roughly 100 homes were swept from their foundations. The storm was forecast to continue moving west over the following days.
stories.headline: Hawaii faces storm damage and power outages after Tropical Storm Lala

stories.body: Lake Powell, the United States' second-largest reservoir, fell to a record-low elevation of 3,519.91 feet above sea level, intensifying concern over the Colorado River system. The lake is more than 20 feet lower than at the start of the year and roughly 30 feet above the level at which its turbines would stop producing hydropower. The milestone followed a record low at Lake Mead and reflects persistent overuse, a very dry winter and rising temperatures. Federal officials and the seven states dependent on the river remain at odds over a long-term management plan, while the Bureau of Reclamation has proposed major potential cuts for Arizona, California and Nevada.
stories.headline: Lake Powell reaches record low, threatening water supplies and hydropower

stories.body: Spain's government said it would open four temporary facilities with space for 1,500 migrants in Ceuta, more than two weeks after a mass crossing left thousands of people in the autonomous city. Migration Minister Elma Saiz said institutional cooperation was needed to restore normality but did not say whether the priority would be returns to Morocco or processing asylum claims, saying measures would follow existing law. The sites include a large parking area near the El Tarajal border, military sports grounds, land near a former factory and an equestrian centre. The move signals a greater focus on emergency accommodation after Morocco tightened control of the border.
stories.headline: Spain creates 1,500 accommodation places for migrants after Ceuta border crisis

stories.body: Ceuta regional president Juan Jesús Vivas has sharply criticised the Spanish government's response to the mass migrant arrival, calling it almost entirely passive and warning that he could seek judicial action if the situation does not change within 30 days. Vivas said thousands of people remained in the city, many living outdoors while awaiting asylum processing or return, and described the situation as unsustainable for public services, security and coexistence. He called for stronger border controls not dependent on Morocco and a new legal framework to speed returns during migration crises. He has also opposed using some central locations and the port for emergency accommodation.
stories.headline: Ceuta's regional president threatens legal action over Spain's migration-crisis response

stories.body: National Court judge Santiago Pedraz has taken over the full investigation into alleged efforts by former Socialist Party member Leire Díez to target the Civil Guard's Central Operational Unit and members of the Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office. Pedraz accepted the transfer of a related Madrid court case, adding 14 volumes of investigative material to his own proceedings. The judges concluded that the two investigations were inseparably linked and should be handled together. The Madrid case had focused on Díez, businessman Javier Pérez Dolset, lawyer Jacobo Teijelo and journalist Pere Rusiñol, while Pedraz's broader inquiry also concerns party figures who may have held more senior roles.
stories.headline: Spain's National Court consolidates investigation into the Leire Díez case

stories.body: Four people aged 18 to 21 were killed and another was seriously injured when a car collided head-on with a truck on the N-122 road near Bulbuente and Maleján, in Zaragoza province. All five occupants of the car were from Zaragoza; the injured person was airlifted to hospital. A second car was involved, but its occupants and the truck driver were unharmed. Firefighters freed victims trapped in the vehicle, and the Civil Guard's traffic-accident investigation unit has opened an inquiry into the circumstances of the collision.
stories.headline: Four young people die in head-on crash in Zaragoza province

stories.body: Barcelona commemorated nine years since the August 2017 attacks on La Rambla and in Cambrils, which killed 16 people and caused physical or psychological harm to at least 352 others. At a ceremony in Plaça Sant Jaume, victim representatives called for authorities to identify and assist those still without compensation. They said 136 people recognised in the National Court ruling have yet to receive payment, and argued that another 125 possible victims identified in the case file should be added. The Catalan victims' association urged anyone who believes they are eligible but has not been compensated to contact it.
stories.headline: Barcelona marks nine years since the 17-A attacks as victims still seek compensation

stories.body: Barcelona began the day under a Meteocat warning for intense nighttime heat, with temperatures reaching 28C in the Raval at 7am and humidity at 76%. Coastal minimum temperatures were forecast at 25C to 27C, while daytime highs in Barcelona were expected to reach 31C to 32C amid heavy, humid conditions and variable cloud. The warning covered Barcelona and other coastal areas, and the city has already recorded a record 52 torrid nights this year at the Les Corts-Can Bruixa station. Forecasters expected another rise in heat before a possible cooler, more unsettled interval later in the week.
stories.headline: Barcelona faces another spell of oppressive heat and a nighttime heat warning

stories.body: An indefinite strike by Groundforce ground staff at Barcelona-El Prat entered its fourteenth day, affecting check-in and baggage services during one of the airport's busiest periods. The stoppage, which began on August 4, has led to 250 flight cancellations and left about 6,000 bags unreturned, with Lufthansa, Air France and KLM among 27 airlines affected. Passengers reported long waits and difficulty recovering luggage. Workers say Groundforce has refused to negotiate over workloads they describe as unsustainable, and the CGT union says the company proposed overtime during the strike despite minimum-service requirements.
stories.headline: Groundforce strike at Barcelona-El Prat enters fourteenth day, disrupting flights and baggage handling

stories.body: A fire in an electrical transformer inside the FNAC store on Barcelona's La Rambla forced the evacuation of the shop on Monday afternoon, but no injuries were reported. Seven fire crews responded, working with the electricity company as authorities closed part of La Rambla and Carrer de Pelai. Accesses to Catalunya metro station on Line 3 at Pelai and La Rambla were temporarily closed, and several bus routes were diverted. Endesa said the fire affected a low-voltage electrical panel serving 17 customers on La Rambla, and a generator was installed to restore supply while repairs were carried out.
stories.headline: Fire at electrical transformer forces evacuation of FNAC store on La Rambla
